_note: Batch E: 6363 IV therapy for migraine, 8929 Texas heat dehydration. Both carry an emergency card in the alert layout, which is deliberately the only full-bleed dark layout in the set: a red-flag list should not look like every other graphic on the page.

cards.subject: migraine
cards.heading: How IV Therapy Helps Relieve Migraines
title: What Is in a
Migraine
IV Drip
cards.alt: A migraine IV drip holds fluids and electrolytes, magnesium, B-complex with anti-nausea, and anti-inflammatories

items.label: Fluids and electrolytes
items.note: Dehydration is a common migraine trigger

items.label: Magnesium
items.note: Frequent migraine sufferers often run low

items.label: B-complex and anti-nausea
items.note: For when pills will not stay down

cards.subject: migraine
cards.heading: Who Can Benefit from IV Therapy for Migraines?
title: Who IV Therapy for
Migraine
Suits
cards.alt: IV migraine therapy suits chronic migraines, dehydration headaches, hormonal episodes, severe nausea and deficiencies

items.label: Chronic migraines
items.note: Where oral medication does not hold

cards.subject: migraine
cards.heading: What to Expect During an IV Migraine Treatment
title: An IV
Migraine
Treatment Visit
cards.alt: An IV migraine treatment: consultation and vitals, a 30 to 60 minute infusion, then back to normal activity

cards.subject: migraine
cards.heading: IV Therapy vs. Traditional Migraine Treatments
title: IV Therapy vs Other
Migraine
Treatments
cards.alt: Oral migraine medication works in 30 to 90 minutes, IV therapy in 15 to 60, preventive drugs work long term

cards.subject: migraine
cards.heading: When to Seek Emergency Care
cards.alt: Migraine red flags needing emergency care: the worst headache of your life, vision loss or slurred speech, confusion or fever
cards.headline: Get help now

signs.text: A sudden, severe headache, the worst of your life
Vision loss, slurred speech, or weakness on one side
Confusion, fever, or a stiff neck

cards.footer: Also seek emergency care for any headache after a head injury

cards.subject: dehydration
cards.heading: Early Warning Signs You Shouldn't Ignore
title: Early Signs of
Dehydration
cards.alt: Early dehydration signs: extreme thirst, urine darker than pale straw, and dizziness or unusual fatigue

items.label: Extreme thirst
items.note: Thirst means you are already behind

items.label: Dark urine
items.note: Pale straw is the target colour

items.label: Dizzy or wiped out
items.note: Low blood volume, heart working harder

cards.subject: dehydration
cards.heading: When Dehydration Becomes a Medical Emergency
cards.alt: Dehydration is an emergency with confusion, a rapid weak pulse, or vomiting that stops you drinking fluids
cards.headline: Get help now

signs.text: Confusion or an altered mental state
Nausea or vomiting that stops you drinking

cards.footer: Also: fainting, severe dizziness, or no sweat despite the heat

cards.subject: IV hydration
cards.heading: Who Needs IV Hydration Therapy Most?
title: Who Needs
IV Hydration
Most in Texas
cards.alt: IV hydration matters most for outdoor workers, athletes, older adults and visitors not acclimatised to Texas heat

items.label: Athletes
items.note: Litres of sweat in one session

cards.subject: dehydration
cards.heading: Proactive Steps to Stay Safe This Summer
title: Staying Ahead of
Dehydration
in the Heat
cards.alt: Prevent dehydration: 16 to 20 ounces four hours before, a cup every 15 to 20 minutes, and stop if you feel off
